outcome.answer: For MoE inference on edge hardware, DyMoE is the closest match: dynamically quantize experts according to their importance, use depth-adaptive scheduling to protect critical layers, and prefetch experts to overlap I/O stalls; it reports lower latency on commercial edge devices [2]. GEMQ instead allocates precision globally across experts and fine-tunes the router to account for routing changes caused by quantization [5]. AlphaQ assigns more bits to experts with stronger heavy-tailed weight spectra, without requiring calibration data [3]. DPA-MoE offers runtime precision control, allocating weight chunks to routed experts according to live gate scores [7]. The supplied abstracts discuss edge inference and efficient MoE quantization, but do not establish performance specifically on mobile hardware [2, 4].
